title: Misery Traverse
lede: A one-way traverse from the western edge of Mudgee, up over Mount Misery and along the ridge to Hill End Road, with big views over town.
description: An 11.9 km one-way traverse from Rifle Range Road on the western edge of Mudgee, over Mount Misery and north along the ridge above Avisford Nature Reserve to Hill End Road near Caerleon.
hero_alt: Topographic map showing the Misery Traverse route from Glen Ayr over Mount Misery and north along the ridge to Hill End Road

card.image_alt: Topographic map of the Misery Traverse route on the western edge of Mudgee
card.blurb: A half-day traverse from the edge of town, up over Mount Misery and along the ridge to Hill End Road. Great views of Mudgee.

facts.label: Region
facts.value: Western edge of Mudgee, Glen Ayr to Caerleon

facts.label: Walk type
facts.value: Fire trail, then partly off-track; One way (car shuffle)

facts.label: Highlights
facts.value: Mount Misery, views over Mudgee, the ridge above Avisford Nature Reserve

intro: Mount Misery is the high ground right on Mudgee's western doorstep. This traverse starts on the edge of town, climbs onto it along the fire trail, then follows the long ridge north above Avisford Nature Reserve to finish on Hill End Road. It takes about half a day, with about 600 m of climbing and great views of Mudgee from up high.

getting_there.intro: This is a one-way walk, so you'll need a car at each end. The start and finish are about 4 km apart in a straight line.

options.heading: Rifle Range Road, Glen Ayr
options.text: The walk starts on Rifle Range Road at Glen Ayr, on the western edge of Mudgee, just west of Faucett Drive. [X: where to park]

options.heading: Hill End Road, Caerleon
options.text: The walk finishes on Hill End Road near the Blain Road turn-off at Caerleon, north-west of town. Leave a car here before you start. [X: where to park]

getting_there.note: The way up crosses private property, so stay on the fire trail. Near the end, head through the tip to keep off private land.

walk_intro: The route heads south from the edge of town on the fire trail to pick up the Mount Misery Trail, climbs over Mount Misery, then follows the ridge north for most of the way to Hill End Road. It's about 600 m of climbing in all. Navigation gets a bit tricky towards the end.

stops.heading: Rifle Range Road
stops.text: Set off from Rifle Range Road at Glen Ayr and head south on the fire trail, away from town and towards the hills. This first part crosses private property, so stay on the fire trail.

stops.heading: Mount Misery Trail
stops.text: Join the Mount Misery Trail and follow it west past the communication tower, where the climb onto Mount Misery begins.

stops.heading: Mount Misery
stops.text: From up high there are great views of Mudgee spread out below. [X: anything else about the top]

stops.heading: The ridge north
stops.text: From Mount Misery, the route follows the long ridge north, keeping west of Avisford Nature Reserve, for about 6 km. [X: views, scrub, rock]

stops.heading: Hill End Road, Caerleon
stops.text:
Towards the end, navigation can be a bit tricky. To keep off private property, head down through the tip to Hill End Road, where your second car is waiting. You may still come across a fence or two.

There's also an exit onto Old Grattai Road, but it goes through private property, so try to avoid it.

tips.heading: Navigation
tips.text: The way up follows fire trails, but navigation gets a bit tricky towards the end. Carry a map and compass or GPS, and know how to use them.

tips.heading: Private land
tips.text: The route crosses private property on the way up, so stay on the fire trail. At the end, head through the tip rather than across private land, and avoid the exit onto Old Grattai Road, which goes through private property. You may come across a fence or two.

tips.heading: Water
tips.text: There's no water on the walk. Carry all you'll need.

tips.heading: Respect the Country
tips.text: This is Wiradjuri Country. Look, but don't touch. Leave no trace.

tips.heading: Tell someone
tips.text: Leave your plans with someone. There's good phone coverage along the way.
